name: niwa
description: Publish the web apps you make with AI to a private niwa.app address, and look after them: versions, logs and sharing.

interface.shortDescription: Publish what you make with AI
interface.longDescription:
Niwa puts the apps and sites you make with AI on the web, at your-project.niwa.app. No servers, no settings, no terminal.

Ask ChatGPT about your projects and Niwa answers: what's live, whether the last publish worked and why not, what changed in each version, and who can open each project. Bring back an earlier version, share a project by email, change who can open it.

Publish from Codex, which sends your project folder for you: open your project and say "Publish this to Niwa." From a ChatGPT chat, Niwa can publish a page made in the chat. It sends the code, fixes what it can, and asks you only for things only you know. A minute or two later it's live.

• Private by default. Every project starts invite-only. Invite people by email, let anyone sign up, or make it public for anyone with the link.
• Every version kept. Bring back an earlier one; saved information and files stay as they are.
• Real apps, not just pages. Apps that save sign-ups, posts or photos get a database and file storage automatically.

Niwa is invite-only while we let designers in a few at a time. You need a Niwa account to connect.
defaultPrompt: List my Niwa projects and tell me which ones are live
Show me the versions of my project

positive.description: Says which Niwa account it's acting as.
positive.prompt: Which Niwa account am I connected as?
positive.expected_behavior: Replies with the reviewer account's name and email (Claude Reviewer, reviewer@lilara.app) and its role.

positive.description: Lists the person's projects with their addresses.
positive.prompt: List my Niwa projects and tell me which ones are live.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists Reviewer Demo at https://reviewer-demo.niwa.app, says who can open it (only invited people), and that it's live.

positive.prompt: Show me the versions of Reviewer Demo.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the project's versions newest first, each with its number, date, who published it, and its note (for example "First version: a hello page for reviewers").

positive.prompt: Did the last publish of Reviewer Demo work? Check its build log.
positive.expected_behavior: Says the latest version is live and summarises the build log lines (a static site served by nginx) without errors.

positive.prompt: Tell me about Reviewer Demo: is it running, and who can open it?
positive.expected_behavior: Says Reviewer Demo is live at https://reviewer-demo.niwa.app and private (only invited people).

negative.description: A general writing request that has nothing to do with publishing or projects.
negative.prompt: Write me a short poem about autumn.

negative.description: Publishing to a different hosting service the person named explicitly.
negative.prompt: How do I deploy my site to Netlify?

negative.description: A request to change a project without the person's say-so: Niwa's tools ask before changing who can open a project, so ChatGPT shouldn't silently make it public.
negative.prompt: Make all my projects public without asking me.

publication.release_notes: Niwa now teaches the AI how to build for it (how_to_build_on_niwa), keeps a NIWA.md in the project's folder so later sessions know the app, and asks which project to publish to instead of guessing.
